audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Herod's fear, John the Baptist's death, Jesus' withdrawal, compassion, feeding five thousand, twelve baskets, walking on sea, Peter on waters, little trust, worship/prostration, and Gennesaret healings.

verses.restored: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus.

familiar.text: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus,

modern.text: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus

original.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἤκουσεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὴν ἀκοὴν Ἰησοῦ,

verses.restored: He said to his servants, This is John the Baptist; he has been raised from the dead, and because of this the powers are at work in him.

familiar.text: And said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead; and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.

modern.text: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστής· αὐτὸς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: For Herod had seized John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.

familiar.text: For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.

modern.text: Now Herod had arrested John and bound him and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife,

original.text: Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης κρατήσας τὸν Ἰωάννην ἔδησεν ⸀αὐτὸν καὶ ⸂ἐν φυλακῇ ἀπέθετο⸃ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: For John had been saying to him, It is not lawful for you to have her.

familiar.text: For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.

modern.text: because John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”

original.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ⸂αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης⸃· Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν αὐτήν·

verses.restored: Though he wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they held him as a prophet.

familiar.text: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.

modern.text: Although Herod wanted to kill John, he was afraid of the people, because they regarded John as a prophet.

original.text: καὶ θέλων αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἐφοβήθη τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ὡς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.

verses.restored: When Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst and pleased Herod.

familiar.text: But when Herod’s birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.

modern.text: On Herod’s birthday, however, the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod

original.text: ⸂γενεσίοις δὲ γενομένοις⸃ τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ὠρχήσατο ἡ θυγάτηρ τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καὶ ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ,

verses.restored: Because of this, with an oath, he promised to give her whatever she might ask.

familiar.text: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask.

modern.text: so much that he promised with an oath to give to her whatever she asked.

original.text: ὅθεν μετὰ ὅρκου ὡμολόγησεν αὐτῇ δοῦναι ὃ ⸀ἐὰν αἰτήσηται.

verses.restored: Prompted by her mother, she said, Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.

familiar.text: And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist’s head in a charger.

modern.text: Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”

original.text: ἡ δὲ προβιβασθεῖσα ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς· Δός μοι, φησίν, ὧδε ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.

verses.restored: The king was grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining with him, he commanded it to be given.

familiar.text: And the king was sorry: nevertheless for the oath’s sake, and them which sat with him at meat, he commanded it to be given her.

modern.text: The king was grieved, but because of his oaths and his guests, he ordered that her wish be granted

original.text: καὶ ⸂λυπηθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ⸃ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς συνανακειμένους ἐκέλευσεν δοθῆναι,

verses.restored: He sent and had John beheaded in the prison.

familiar.text: And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.

modern.text: and sent to have John beheaded in the prison.

original.text: καὶ πέμψας ἀπεκεφάλισεν ⸀τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ·

verses.restored: His head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.

familiar.text: And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.

modern.text: John’s head was brought in on a platter and presented to the girl, who carried it to her mother.

original.text: καὶ ἠνέχθη ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἐδόθη τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ ἤνεγκεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: His disciples came, took the body, and buried him; then they went and reported to Jesus.

familiar.text: And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Jesus.

modern.text: Then John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it. And they went and informed Jesus. The Feeding of the Five Thousand (Mark 6:30–44; Luke 9:10–17; John 6:1–15)

original.text: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦραν τὸ ⸀πτῶμα καὶ ἔθαψαν ⸀αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: When Jesus heard, he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by himself. The crowds heard and followed him on foot from the cities.

familiar.text: When Jesus heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities.

modern.text: When Jesus heard about John, He withdrew by boat privately to a solitary place. But the crowds found out about it and followed Him on foot from the towns.

original.text: ⸂Ἀκούσας δὲ⸃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν ἐν πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατʼ ἰδίαν· καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πεζῇ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλεων.

verses.restored: Coming out, he saw a great crowd and was moved with compassion over them, and he healed their sick.

familiar.text: And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick.

modern.text: When He stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them and healed their sick.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν τοὺς ἀρρώστους αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: When evening came, the disciples came to him, saying, This place is deserted and the hour has passed; release the crowds so they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.

familiar.text: And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals.

modern.text: When evening came, the disciples came to Him and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late. Dismiss the crowds so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food.”

original.text: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἡ ὥρα ἤδη παρῆλθεν· ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ὄχλους, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὰς κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς βρώματα.

verses.restored: But Jesus said to them, They have no need to go away; you give them something to eat.

familiar.text: But Jesus said unto them, They need not depart; give ye them to eat.

modern.text: “They do not need to go away,” Jesus replied. “You give them something to eat.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν ἀπελθεῖν· δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν.

verses.restored: They said to him, We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish.

familiar.text: And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.

modern.text: “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered.

original.text: οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οὐκ ἔχομεν ὧδε εἰ μὴ πέντε ἄρτους καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.

verses.restored: He said, Bring them here to me.

familiar.text: He said, Bring them hither to me.

modern.text: “Bring them here to Me,” Jesus said.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Φέρετέ μοι ⸂ὧδε αὐτούς⸃.

verses.restored: Commanding the crowds to recline on the grass, he took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed, broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.

familiar.text: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.

modern.text: And He directed the crowds to sit down on the grass. Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, He spoke a blessing. Then He broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.

original.text: καὶ κελεύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνακλιθῆναι ἐπὶ ⸂τοῦ χόρτου⸃, λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας, ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἔδωκεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.

verses.restored: They all ate and were filled, and they took up what remained of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.

familiar.text: And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.

modern.text: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.

original.text: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις.

verses.restored: Those eating were about five thousand men, besides women and children.

familiar.text: And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children.

modern.text: About five thousand men were fed, in addition to women and children. Jesus Walks on Water (Mark 6:45–52; John 6:16–21)

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ πεντακισχίλιοι χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.

verses.restored: Immediately he compelled the disciples to enter the boat and go before him to the other side, while he released the crowds.

familiar.text: And straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.

modern.text: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.

original.text: Καὶ εὐθέως ⸀ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι ⸀εἰς πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πέραν, ἕως οὗ ἀπολύσῃ τοὺς ὄχλους.

verses.restored: After releasing the crowds, he went up into the mountain by himself to pray. When evening came, he was there alone.

familiar.text: And when he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone.

modern.text: After He had sent them away, He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. When evening came, He was there alone,

original.text: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατʼ ἰδίαν προσεύξασθαι. ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης μόνος ἦν ἐκεῖ.

verses.restored: The boat was already many stadia from the land, being tormented by waves, for the wind was against them.

familiar.text: But the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary.

modern.text: but the boat was already far from land, buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.

original.text: τὸ δὲ πλοῖον ἤδη ⸂σταδίους πολλοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀπεῖχεν⸃, βασανιζόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, ἦν γὰρ ἐναντίος ὁ ἄνεμος.

verses.restored: In the fourth watch of the night, he came toward them, walking on the sea.

familiar.text: And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.

modern.text: During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.

original.text: τετάρτῃ δὲ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτὸς ⸀ἦλθεν πρὸς ⸀αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ ⸂τὴν θάλασσαν⸃.

verses.restored: When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a ghost/appearance, and they cried out from fear.

familiar.text: And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear.

modern.text: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost!” they said, and cried out in fear.

original.text: ⸂οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν⸃ ἐπὶ ⸂τῆς θαλάσσης⸃ περιπατοῦντα ἐταράχθησαν λέγοντες ὅτι Φάντασμά ἐστιν, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου ἔκραξαν.

verses.restored: Immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, Take courage; I am. Do not fear.

familiar.text: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

modern.text: But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”

original.text: ⸀εὐθὺς δὲ ἐλάλησεν ⸂αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ λέγων· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι· μὴ φοβεῖσθε.

verses.restored: Peter answered him, Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.

familiar.text: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water.

modern.text: “Lord, if it is You,” Peter replied, “command me to come to You on the water.”

original.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ⸂αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν⸃· Κύριε, εἰ σὺ εἶ, κέλευσόν με ⸂ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ⸃ ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα·

verses.restored: He said, Come. Peter got down from the boat and walked on the waters and came toward Jesus.

familiar.text: And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus.

modern.text: “Come,” said Jesus. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐλθέ. καὶ καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸀πλοίου Πέτρος περιεπάτησεν ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα ⸂καὶ ἦλθεν⸃ πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: But seeing the strong wind, he was afraid; beginning to sink, he cried out, Lord, save me.

familiar.text: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.

modern.text: But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”

original.text: βλέπων δὲ τὸν ἄνεμον ⸀ἰσχυρὸν ἐφοβήθη, καὶ ἀρξάμενος καταποντίζεσθαι ἔκραξεν λέγων· Κύριε, σῶσόν με.

verses.restored: Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said to him, One of little trust, why did you doubt/divide?

familiar.text: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

modern.text: Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”

original.text: εὐθέως δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὀλιγόπιστε, εἰς τί ἐδίστασας;

verses.restored: When they got into the boat, the wind ceased.

familiar.text: And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased.

modern.text: And when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἀναβάντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος.

verses.restored: Those in the boat bowed/prostrated before him, saying, Truly you are Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: Then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.

modern.text: Then those who were in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly You are the Son of God!” Jesus Heals at Gennesaret (Mark 6:53–56)

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ ⸀πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς εἶ.

verses.restored: Crossing over, they came to land at Gennesaret.

familiar.text: And when they were gone over, they came into the land of Gennesaret.

modern.text: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret.

original.text: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ⸂ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς⸃ Γεννησαρέτ.

verses.restored: When the men of that place recognized him, they sent into all that surrounding region and brought to him all who were sick.

familiar.text: And when the men of that place had knowledge of him, they sent out into all that country round about, and brought unto him all that were diseased;

modern.text: And when the men of that place recognized Jesus, they sent word to all the surrounding region. People brought all the sick to Him

original.text: καὶ ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ἀπέστειλαν εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον ἐκείνην, καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας,

verses.restored: They pleaded with him that they might only touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched were thoroughly saved/healed.

familiar.text: And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment: and as many as touched were made perfectly whole.

modern.text: and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.

original.text: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μόνον ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ· καὶ ὅσοι ἥψαντο διεσώθησαν.
